_comment: Delivering the dead god's letter to the Hearth-Turner. The third god-questline opener.
THE LOCKED SOURCE, again the letter itself, which shipped before this scene existed:
SUBJECT: TEMPORAL AUTHORITY -- request for a copy
'You will have kept it. You keep all of them. I am asking for the version where I
was wrong, and I am asking because I no longer have it and I have looked.'
'Send it as it was filed. Do not correct it on my account. I am aware that asking
you not to correct a record is its own kind of request.'
WORLD.md: 'The Hearth-Turner / Ash -- the one who kept every version of the argument.
A god whose law is memory has never let a grievance become past tense. It holds the
family's entire falling-out, in order, and will show you. That makes it the exposition
god, but earned: it is not telling you because the plot needs it told, it is telling
you because it has never been able to stop.'
SO THE EXPOSITION HAS TO BE SOMETHING THE PLAYER CAN TURN OFF, and that is the whole
design of this file. A god that cannot stop talking is only characterization if the
player is the one who has to stop it. Letting it run is generous and costs you time;
cutting it off is reasonable and costs you nothing you can see. Neither is punished.
The lore is available and never compulsory -- which is also the only honest way to
ship an exposition scene without it becoming a lore dump with dialogue options.
THE BEAT IS THAT THE COPY IS ALREADY READY. It has been ready. Nobody ever asked, so
it was never sent, and the one who finally asked is dead -- so the request arrives at
a god who can fulfil it perfectly and has nowhere to send it.
THE UNANIMOUS NODE IS ASKING IT TO HAND THE COPY OVER, and it is deliberately NOT the
same transgression as the other two scenes. The Verdant's is taking away a defence;
the Anchorite's is telling it the job is over. For a god whose entire law is that
nothing is ever finished and nothing is ever lost, the unthinkable thing is letting a
record LEAVE. Three gods, three different unbearable requests, and none of them is
'be sad about your relative'.
THE NAME IS NOT IN THIS FILE. `tools/letters_check.py` asserts the three names appear
in their own letters and nowhere else in the shipped string table.
Dread covenant: the grief is sincere throughout and never the punchline. The permitted
comedy is the SYSTEM -- a request for a copy, a filing reference, an office that can
produce any version of anything except the one where it is over.
Regard: HEARTH_TURNER throughout, and the most generous route is worth +30 against the
post-deicide floor of -45. `dialogue_check.py` now refuses any scene whose best route
would pass the -10 ceiling, because `adjust` clamps and the tail of such a scene pays
a capped player nothing.
